question: What will be US total vehicle sales, not seasonally adjusted (BEA) for August 2026, as first published?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the first published value of US total vehicle sales, not seasonally adjusted (BEA) for August 2026 (FRED series TOTALNSA). Later revisions are ignored.

research:
## 1. Resolution source

- 2026-08-14: The question resolves on FRED series TOTALNSA (BEA Total Vehicle Sales, not seasonally adjusted, thousands of units). Per the code-collected baseline, the latest observation as of today is **1402.982 for July 2026**. [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/data/TOTALNSA.txt)
- Recent history from FRED, in thousands: Jan-26 1116.7, Feb-26 1206.3, Mar-26 1430.9, Apr-26 1421.9, May-26 1522.6, Jun-26 1423.1, Jul-26 about 1403. August in past years: Aug-23 1365.0, Aug-24 1457.2, Aug-25 1500.4. [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/data/TOTALNSA.txt)
- BEA's total includes heavy trucks. It usually comes in about 3% above industry light-vehicle counts. For example, July 2026 was 1.36M light vehicles (Cox/Mercer) against 1403k in BEA's series.

## 2. Current status

- Nothing settles the question yet. August sales are reported at the start of September, and BEA/FRED should publish around Sep 2-4.
- Calendar: August 2026 starts on a Saturday and has 5 Sundays and no holiday, so it has **26 selling days**. That is one fewer than August 2025, whose count included the Labor Day weekend (Labor Day was Sep 1, 2025). In 2026 Labor Day is Sep 7, so the holiday weekend falls in September's reporting period. This points to lower raw volume than Aug-25's 1500k even if the selling pace stays flat. I worked out the day count myself; no source dated on or before 8/14 confirmed it.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)

- 2026-08-14: Mercer Capital says the July SAAR fell 1.4% to 16.3M from 16.6M in June. Unadjusted volume was about 1.36M, down 1.5% year over year, the fifth yearly decline in seven months. Mercer expects the August SAAR to stay "near the mid-16 million range." Other points: average incentives about $3,451, up 8.1% from a year earlier; a record July monthly payment of $808; and demand, not supply, is now the limiting factor. [Mercer](https://mercercapital.com/insights/blogs/auto-dealer-valuation-insights-blog/2026/july-2026-saar/)
- About 2026-08-04: Cox's July update put sales at 1.36M with a 16.3M SAAR. That was below pre-release forecasts of 16.5 to 16.9M (Cox had forecast 16.7M). [Cox July forecast](https://www.coxautoinc.com/insights/cox-automotive-forecast-july-2026-us-auto-sales-forecast/), [CollisionWeek](https://collisionweek.com/2026/07/27/july-new-vehicle-sales-pace-highest-selling-rate-2026/)
- About 2026-07-23: Omdia expected July at about 1.389M (16.6M SAAR) with inventory rebuilding to 49 days. It said "August is expected to ease modestly," citing high borrowing costs and rising gas prices. [Omdia](https://omdia.tech.informa.com/om146133/us-light-vehicle-sales-flat-yoy-in-july-inventory-builds-to-49-days)

## 4. Base rates

- Code baseline from 1-month changes off July's 1403: p5 1041, p10 1148, p25 1291, **p50 1415**, p75 1573, p90 1674, p95 1760. This spread is too wide for an August-specific estimate, because July-to-August moves are seasonal and fairly stable.
- July-to-August change in past years:
  - 2023: 1339.9 to 1365.0, +1.9%
  - 2024: 1328.9 to 1457.2, +9.7% (August had extra selling days, and July was hit by the CDK cyberattack)
  - 2025: 1425.7 to 1500.4, +5.2% (27 selling days in August)
- Rough arithmetic, not a forecast:
  - A 16.3 to 16.5M SAAR over 26 days implies about 1.33 to 1.37M light vehicles. Adding about 3% for heavy trucks gives roughly 1.37 to 1.41M on BEA's basis.
  - Each 0.5M change in SAAR moves the monthly unadjusted figure by about 40k.
  - Fewer selling days make a year-over-year decline from 1500k likely.
- The July figure may be revised before the August value is first published. First-published values have sometimes differed from later FRED values by small amounts, roughly ±10k.

## 5. Other forecasts

- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on this series.
- Cox Automotive and J.D. Power/GlobalData usually publish their August forecasts around Aug 25-27, after the question closes, so none was available as of 2026-08-14.
- The only expert outlooks published by today:
  - Mercer: August SAAR in the mid-16M range. [Mercer](https://mercercapital.com/insights/blogs/auto-dealer-valuation-insights-blog/2026/july-2026-saar/)
  - Omdia: August "expected to ease modestly." [Omdia](https://omdia.tech.informa.com/om145796/us-light-vehicle-sales--inventory-forecast--august-2026)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution

- About Aug 25-27: Cox and J.D. Power/GlobalData publish their August forecasts (after the question closes).
- Sep 1-3: automakers report August sales, followed by Wards/Motor Intelligence estimates and the BEA/FRED update around Sep 2-4.
- Other factors that could move the number:
  - Gas prices pushing buyers toward hybrids
  - Interest rates and incentive levels
  - Whether dealers pull Labor Day promotions forward into late August
  - Any tariff or price changes when 2027 model-year vehicles roll out

Sources: [FRED TOTALNSA](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/data/TOTALNSA.txt), [Mercer Capital July 2026 SAAR](https://mercercapital.com/insights/blogs/auto-dealer-valuation-insights-blog/2026/july-2026-saar/), [Cox July 2026 forecast](https://www.coxautoinc.com/insights/cox-automotive-forecast-july-2026-us-auto-sales-forecast/), [CollisionWeek](https://collisionweek.com/2026/07/27/july-new-vehicle-sales-pace-highest-selling-rate-2026/), [Omdia July](https://omdia.tech.informa.com/om146133/us-light-vehicle-sales-flat-yoy-in-july-inventory-builds-to-49-days), [Omdia August forecast listing](https://omdia.tech.informa.com/om145796/us-light-vehicle-sales--inventory-forecast--august-2026)
